text:
ellen_support: Heads-up — customer reported a nightly bulk embed job hitting 429s and occasional "dimension mismatch" errors. Job: ~50k texts, sent as 200-request batches via our embeddings endpoint. They say failures started at ~02:10 UTC last night. Logs attached: s3://redwood-support-uploads/acme/embed-run-202403.avro
ellen_support: snippet from their client error (copied):
```json
{"error": "429 Too Many Requests", "message": "rate limit exceeded"}
```
and separately:
```json
{"error": "400 Bad Request", "message": "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024"}
```
raju_sre: Thanks — do we have request-level logs (route, model, concurrency)? Also want the exact model name the customer passed. 429s = rate limit/burst window; dimension 400s = wrong model or mixed-model batch.
ellen_support: customer says model param = "text-embed-small-v2" in their code. They send 200 items per request and run ~16 parallel workers overnight. I asked for a small repro bundle; they uploaded a 1000-item sample to the same S3 bucket.
maria_ml: If their workers are mixing model names or reusing a client with a different pinned model, you can get dimension mismatch when downstream we route to a different model family. Two quick checks:
- confirm model param per-request (server logs show what we routed) — raju, can you grep for thread id 0x9f in the logs? 
- check that the embedding vector length they assert matches the model spec (e.g., text-embed-small-v2 => 768 dims; larger variants => 1536).
raju_sre: I pulled the route logs. Most of their requests hit model id text-embed-small-v2 (768d) but ~12% of requests were routed to text-embed-large (1536d) because they were using a model alias that maps to multiple backends for rollouts. That explains the dimension mismatch when they mixed batch elements originating from different workers.
raju_sre: The 429s were correlated with bursts at minute boundaries — they had 16 workers each sending 1 request every ~4s, plus our internal batching spikes. This exceeded their per-minute request cap (burst window). I recommend these mitigations:
- reduce parallel workers to 8 for nightly bulk
- set batch_size <= 256
- implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429
maria_ml: Also recommend pinning an explicit model version rather than the alias until rollouts complete, e.g., model: text-embed-small-v2@20240301. That prevents cross-variant mixes.
ellen_support: Can we give a simple backoff snippet for the customer? They asked for code.
raju_sre: Sure — python example I often send:
```python
import time, random

def backoff(attempt):
    base = 0.5
    return base * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 0.5)

for attempt in range(6):
    resp = client.embeddings.create(...)
    if resp.status_code == 429:
        sleep = backoff(attempt)
        time.sleep(sleep)
        continue
    break
```
Recommend jitter in ms and cap concurrency.
maria_ml: For reproducing the 429 locally: run a script that fires 10 parallel processes, each sending 1000-item requests (or smaller requests but high concurrency) to mimic their pattern. Also simulate alias mixing by alternating model param values.
ellen_support: I added these recommendations to the support ticket and asked them to lower concurrency and pin model version. Customer asked if we can temporarily raise their burst quota for this nightly job window.
raju_sre: I can temporarily raise burst allowance for that customer tenant for the next 12 hours. Will do one-off change and monitor. @deploy-bot can you apply a transient quota bump to tenant acme-inc: +2x burst for 12h? Include a rollback timer.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: executed change request #INC-2024-9876: applied transient quota bump +2x burst to tenant acme-inc, window 12h. Monitoring enabled. Rollback scheduled in 12 hours.
ellen_support: Awesome — I told the customer we've applied a temporary bump and shared the backoff snippet + pin-model advice. They also asked for a short-term workaround if they can't change their code tonight.
maria_ml: Short term workaround: reduce each worker's batch size to 64 and add a 50–150ms random sleep between requests to avoid synchronized bursts. Also avoid mixing aliases.
raju_sre: I'll keep streaming the logs to the support ticket and will escalate to infra if 429s persist after the bump.
ellen_support: Closing loop here — follow-up items:
- raju: monitor the tenant for 6 hrs and report metrics (429 rate, mean latency)
- maria_ml: send a note to the model-ops team to delay alias rollouts for customers with large bulk jobs
- ellen_support: confirm the customer can resume the nightly job with suggested changes and update the ticket.
ellen_support: Thanks all :pray:
